notes: I could not extract text from the UKAS schedule PDFs, so I have no lab counts. This session had no Bash or Python tool, so pypdf was unavailable. The Read tool needs pdftoppm, which isn't installed. WebFetch returns only PDF metadata for the compressed schedules: 8993 is a single-site schedule with metadata dated 2025-10-24. A web search confirmed that schedule PDFs are public and reachable without a login. Known public schedule numbers or URLs: 8092 (Exeter genomics lab), 8840 (Cambridge East GLH), 9865 (NW GLH Manchester), 9322 (NW GLH Liverpool), 20634, 8127, 29022, plus inab.ie/fileupload/medical-testing/genseq-diagnostics-421mt.pdf for Irish INAB. The source looks reachable and potentially useful, but only if text can be extracted locally.
how_to_mine: Run this from a shell with Python. Create a fresh empty directory. Download each PDF from https://www.ukas.com/download-schedule/{no}/Medical (or /Testing) using curl or requests. Candidate numbers are 8523, 8993, 8727, 20372, 8092, 8840, 9865, 9322, 8127, 20634, 29022 and 29671. Add the other GLH accreditation numbers from each hub's accreditation page. Run python -I with pypdf to extract text. Regex for 'NovaSeq( ?6000| ?X| ?X Plus)?', 'NextSeq', 'HiSeq', and the 'Issue No.' and 'Issue date' header fields. Tabulate per lab: 6000 only, X only, or both, and the issue date. Re-fetch periodically to catch new issue numbers, or use the Wayback Machine for older issues to date when each lab adds the X and drops the 6000. Repeat for INAB (inab.ie/fileupload/medical-testing/*.pdf) and DAkkS (akkreditierung.dakks.de, search for 'NovaSeq').
new_candidates: Medical University of Graz human genetics has a NovaSeq X Plus under EN/ISO 15189 (forschungsinfrastruktur.bmfwf.gv.at id=6458): a clinical lab already on the X, which is a data point against a long tail there.
INAB Ireland medical-testing PDFs, for example genseq-diagnostics-421mt.pdf
